facts.text: Damian asked the assistant to remember all the details about Damian and Damian's writing style.
Damian wrote an application titled "The Design and Implementation of Nano Neural Interfaces".
Damian plans to conduct further research into nanotransducers as a means of a functional neural interface (FNI).
Damian's proposed study evaluates the properties of different nanotransducers and whether they are suitable for an FNI system.
Damian's research plan involves building on a recent study about nano-functional interfaces that improve electrodes, image neurons, and stimulate neurons.
Damian plans to investigate nFNIs (nano-functional neural interfaces) that showed the most potential in the referenced study.
Damian plans to explore which nFNI(s) would be optimal for a communication relay between other transducers.

Damian's current hypothesis is that a combination of specialized imaging transducers, specialized stimulation transducers, and specialized relay transducers would be needed for stable bidirectional communication with the brain.
Damian plans to use Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans) as the model system in the investigation.
Damian chose C. elegans because of the complete understanding of its genome and connectome.
Damian's study aims for nanotransducer placement that is stable yet reversible.
Damian notes that nanotransducers could be transported into neurons, which would hinder removal and potentially be toxic to the cell.
Damian's study has three objectives: imaging neurons, stimulating neurons, and relaying signals.
Damian's objective 1 is to find the optimal method for imaging individual neurons on an individual level.
Damian plans to investigate quantum dot imaging, voltage-sensitive dye imaging, and genetically encoded voltage indicators for imaging neurons.
Damian hypothesizes that genetically encoded voltage indicators will be the most effective method for signaling neuronal activity.
Damian plans to use patch-clamp and calcium imaging as controls for the imaging experiment.
Damian's objective 2 is to find the optimal method for minimally invasive stimulation of neurons.
Damian proposes using nFNIs as an alternative for electrode-based stimulation to bypass invasiveness.
Damian expects that due to their size, it would take multiple nFNIs to receive the signal for the neuron to fire.
Damian expects that neuron modulation would be enough to make the neuron fire consistently without damaging the cell.
Damian plans to compare magnetoelectric, piezoelectric, and optoelectric nanotransducers to test whether nFNIs are suitable for neurostimulation.
Damian plans to use a giant squid axon as the recipient of stimulation in the stimulation experiment.
Damian states that C. elegans will not be used in the stimulation experiment to control for potential discrepancies in behavior between trials.
Damian plans to use a microelectrode as the baseline for the stimulation experiment to measure nFNIs against conventional stimulation methods.
Damian's objective 3 is to determine whether nFNIs can be used as signal relays.
Damian hypothesizes that nFNIs can be used as a relay system to send and receive external devices' signals.
Damian describes an imaging nFNI receiving information of a neuron firing and transducing the signal, then a nearby relay nFNI relaying the signal until it reaches the skull.
Damian describes the process conversely for signals sent to the specific neuron.
Damian plans to immobilize C. elegans in the relay experiment.
Damian plans to place a material embedded with the nFNI being tested on top of C. elegans to simulate human tissue and bone.
Damian plans to implement the optimal imaging method and stimulation method from the previous experiments in the relay experiment.
Damian plans to compare the relayed signals to the actual signals to assess feasibility.
Damian aims to further the state of the art of functional neural interfaces by introducing a potentially minimally invasive, biocompatible neural interface.
Damian references DARPA's "Next-Generation Nonsurgical Neurotechnology" as evidence the field is heading toward improved bidirectional communication with neurons.
Damian's broader impacts include increasing medical imaging of the brain if the system is proved feasible.
Damian states that increased brain imaging could help diagnose neurological disorders such as Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease, and epilepsy.
Damian states that if single neurons could be stimulated on a whole-brain level, the system may be used to treat those disorders more efficiently without the need for surgeries.
Damian states that nFNIs as relays could help traditional non-invasive imaging methods such as electroencephalogram by bringing signals from deeper within the brain toward the scalp.
Damian's long-term goal is to build a bidirectional neural interface.
Damian states that more information is needed on neural dynamics to understand how modulating neurons may affect the system as a whole.
Damian suggests a future study may involve training a neural decoder with the behavior of a model.
Damian suggests that Damian would attempt to stimulate neurons in the model to repeat the observed behavior.
Damian states that artificial intelligence could be utilized to build the optimal decoder using a means of receiving input from neurons and giving output to them.
